message: docs(agents): a checkpoint preserves what it names, or it names nothing

edits.find: A slice that ended without a checkpoint is incomplete rather than merely unfinished.
edits.replace:
A slice that ended without a checkpoint is incomplete rather than merely unfinished.

A checkpoint names what is prepared, and naming it does not preserve it. Anything that would otherwise die with your session goes somewhere durable before you write the checkpoint, and the checkpoint links it: a generated `.ai/edits` request you ran out of room to submit, a parsed error inventory that cost several round trips to assemble, a script that produces either, a measurement nobody should have to take twice. A gist is where that goes, and the link belongs in the checkpoint comment rather than in this repository, because none of it is repository content, none of it is evidence, and a second copy inside the tree would be a second owner of the state `docs/SESSION-STATUS.md` owns. Prefer the artifact that regenerates the work to the work itself: a request pins `expected_head` and one blob SHA per path, so it expires at the next publication, while the script that builds it does not. Say who it is for, because nothing in a gist can be dispatched through `.ai/edits`, which refuses shell commands and unknown operations by design. And say what is not claimed about it, at minimum that it has no run in this repository's suite and that its output is reviewed rather than trusted, on the same rule that keeps a prepared candidate from being read as a published commit. Three requests covering 47 files and 103 edits were generated and then lost exactly this way on #453, and the next implementor inherited a single next action that no longer pointed at anything.
